name: TL062CDR
title: Low-power JFET-input operational amplifiers, single, dual and quad (TL061, TL062, TL064)
summary: TL061, TL062 and TL064 are one, two and four JFET-input op amps that need about 200 µA per amplifier. They run from ±5 V to ±15 V, give 1 MHz unity-gain bandwidth and 3.5 V/µs slew rate, and have input bias currents of tens of picoamps. Compensation is internal, the output is short-circuit protected and the common-mode range takes in the positive supply. TL062CDR is the dual, C grade (0 °C to 70 °C), in SOIC-8 on tape and reel.
key_figures: 200 µA typ, 250 µA max per amplifier
±5 V to ±15 V recommended, ±18 V absolute
±13.5 V typ into 10 kΩ on ±15 V

circuits.title: Single-pole low-pass filter
circuits.description: R1 and C1 form a low-pass section at the non-inverting input; RF from output to inverting input and RG from the inverting input to ground set the passband gain, 1 + RF / RG. The corner is f-3dB = 1 / (2π × R1 × C1).
notes: Supply connections are not drawn.

circuits.title: Inverting amplifier, gain -3.6
circuits.description: One amplifier inverts and scales its input: RI feeds the inverting input, RF closes the loop from the output and the non-inverting input is grounded. With RI = 10 kΩ and RF = 36 kΩ the gain is -3.6, turning a ±0.5 V signal into about ±1.8 V. The supply is ±12 V, wider than both the input and output swings. The second amplifier is not used.
notes: The input source returns to GND.

circuits.title: Instrumentation amplifier with one TL064
circuits.description: Sections 1 and 2 are followers driven from inputs A and B through 100 kΩ each. Their outputs feed section 3 through 10 kΩ, 0.1 % resistors: on the A side a second 10 kΩ, 0.1 % resistor goes from the inverting input to ground; on the B side the second one goes from the non-inverting input to the output of section 4. Section 4 has 100 kΩ from its non-inverting input to ground, 100 kΩ from its output to its inverting input, and a 1 MΩ variable resistor from its inverting input to the circuit output.

parts.note: potentiometer, wiper tied to the output end

notes: Sections 1 and 2 are the input buffers, 3 the output stage and 4 the gain-setting inverter.

circuits.title: 0.5 Hz square-wave oscillator
circuits.description: RF (100 kΩ) runs from the output to CF (3.3 µF) to ground; the inverting input is fed from the RF-CF junction through 3.3 kΩ. The output goes through 1 kΩ to a node with 9.1 kΩ to ground, and that node feeds the non-inverting input through 3.3 kΩ. f = 1 / (2π × RF × CF) gives 0.5 Hz. Supplies are +15 V and -15 V.

circuits.title: High-Q notch filter, 1 kHz
circuits.description: A twin-T network ahead of a voltage follower. R1 and R2 in series carry C3 from their junction, and C1 and C2 in series carry R3 from their junction; C3 and R3 return to the follower output. With R1 = R2 = 2 × R3 = 1.5 MΩ and C1 = C2 = C3 / 2 = 110 pF, fO = 1 kHz.
notes: The source returns to the circuit ground.

circuits.title: Audio-distribution amplifier
circuits.description: Single supply. The input reaches the first section's non-inverting input through 1 µF. That section has 1 MΩ from output to inverting input and 100 kΩ from the inverting input to a bias node; a resistor with no value given joins the non-inverting input to the same node. The bias node sits on a 100 kΩ / 100 kΩ divider from VCC+ to ground with 100 µF to ground. Three followers, each driven from the first section's output, give outputs A, B and C.
notes: The resistor from the non-inverting input to the bias node carries no value.

circuits.title: Low-level light detector preamplifier
circuits.description: A TIL601 phototransistor with 10 kΩ from collector to +15 V and 5 kΩ from emitter to ground feeds the non-inverting input from its collector through 10 kΩ. A 10 kΩ potentiometer between two 10 kΩ resistors across +15 V and -15 V feeds the inverting input from its wiper through 10 kΩ. 100 pF joins the two inputs.

circuits.title: AC amplifier
circuits.description: Single supply, inverting. The input drives the inverting input through 10 kΩ, with 1 MΩ from output to inverting input. The non-inverting input sits on a 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider from VCC+ to ground with 0.1 µF to ground, and is the input return; 50 Ω joins the two input lines. A 250 kΩ potentiometer spans OFFSET N1 and N2 with its wiper to ground. 0.1 µF goes from VCC+ to ground.

circuits.title: Microphone preamplifier with tone control
circuits.description: The microphone reaches the non-inverting input through 0.1 µF, with 47 kΩ to ground. The inverting input has 100 kΩ to ground, 270 Ω in series with 20 µF to ground, and 2.7 kΩ to a feedback node; that node has 1.2 MΩ to the output and 0.003 µF to a second node, which has 100 kΩ to the output and 0.001 µF to the output. The output drives a tone network through 1 µF: a 100 kΩ potentiometer with 0.06 µF capacitors, a 50 kΩ potentiometer with 0.002 µF and 0.02 µF, and resistors of 10 kΩ, 1 kΩ, 100 kΩ and 10 kΩ; a 50 kΩ variable resistor leads to the output terminal.

parts.note: potentiometer, wiper tied to the output end

notes: Supply voltages are not specified.

circuits.title: Instrumentation amplifier with one TL062
circuits.description: A two-amplifier instrumentation amplifier. IN+ drives the first section's non-inverting input; 100 kΩ joins its output to its inverting input. That inverting input connects through 1 kΩ to the second section's output, which also has 1 kΩ to the second section's inverting input; that input has 100 kΩ to ground. IN- drives the second section's non-inverting input.
notes: Supply voltages are not specified.

circuits.title: Input offset-voltage null, TL061
circuits.description: A 100 kΩ potentiometer across OFFSET N1 and N2 with its wiper returned to VCC- through 1.5 kΩ trims the input offset voltage of the single TL061.

circuits.title: Unity-gain amplifier test circuit
circuits.description: The slew-rate, rise-time and overshoot measurements use a voltage follower loaded by 2 kΩ and 100 pF in parallel to ground.

circuits.title: Gain-of-10 inverting amplifier test circuit
circuits.description: An inverting stage with 1 kΩ input and 10 kΩ feedback resistors, loaded by RL and 100 pF to ground.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier
circuits.description: VIN reaches the non-inverting input through RIN; RG runs from the inverting input to ground and RF from the output to the inverting input.
notes: Supply connections are not drawn on the schematic; the matching board layout bypasses VCC+ to ground with a ceramic capacitor, and VCC- too on split supplies.

circuits.title: IC preamplifier with bass and treble controls
circuits.description: Two sections of one TL062. The input reaches the first section's - input through 1 µF, with 47 kΩ and 50 pF to ground. A network from the first section's output returns to its + input: 220 kΩ, 0.00375 µF, and 0.01 µF in series with 27 kΩ, all in parallel; the same + input has 100 Ω, a 100 Ω balance variable resistor and 75 µF in series to ground. The first section's output drives a 5 kΩ gain potentiometer to ground; its wiper feeds, through 47 µF, a bass and treble network (100 kΩ bass and 100 kΩ treble potentiometers, 10 kΩ, 3.3 kΩ, 0.03 µF and 0.003 µF parts) that is also fed from the output and returns to the second section's + input. The second section's - input has 68 kΩ to ground.

operation.text: TL061 is a single, TL062 a dual and TL064 a quad JFET-input op amp. They correspond to the TL07x and TL08x families at lower power consumption, about 200 µA per amplifier. A and B grades have tighter offset limits than the standard grade; the suffix gives the temperature range: C 0 °C to 70 °C, I -40 °C to 85 °C, M -55 °C to 125 °C (Q -40 °C to 125 °C in the operating conditions).

The input stage is JFET; input impedance is high and input bias and offset currents are low. Frequency compensation is internal and the output stage is class AB. EMI and RF filtering is built in. The parts are free of latch-up.

On ±15 V the common-mode input range reaches from -12 V to 15 V typically, so it includes VCC+, with ±11 V guaranteed. The output swings ±13.5 V typically into 10 kΩ, ±10 V minimum. The recommended common-mode range is VCC- + 4 V to VCC+ - 4 V.
Unity-gain bandwidth is 1 MHz and slew rate 3.5 V/µs typical. Common-mode rejection ratio is 86 dB typical.
The bias current of the JFET inputs is junction leakage and rises steeply with temperature: about 30 pA typical at 25 °C and close to 30 nA at 125 °C.
There is no enable: the amplifiers run as soon as supply is applied. They work from one supply or from split supplies.
The output is protected and may stay shorted to ground or either supply indefinitely, as long as the package dissipation is kept within its rating.

More than 36 V on a single supply, or more than ±18 V on split supplies, can destroy the part. A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor sits close to each supply pin to reduce errors coupled in from noisy or high-impedance supplies.

Low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitors go from each supply pin to ground right at the device; one from V+ is enough on a single supply. Keep analog and digital grounds apart and use a ground plane, which also spreads heat and cuts EMI pickup. Route inputs away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles when they must meet. Keep the gain resistors next to the inverting input and the input traces short. A driven guard ring around sensitive nodes reduces leakage.

In the non-inverting example on an 8-pin single, RG and RF sit right at the inverting input pin, RIN at the non-inverting pin, a ceramic bypass capacitor at VCC+ and another at VCC- (only for split supplies), with a ground plane on another layer.

The inverting amplifier scales ±0.5 V to ±1.8 V, a gain of -3.6. The supply has to exceed the input and output ranges; ±12 V is enough. Resistors in the kilohm range hold the circuit currents to milliamps: RI = 10 kΩ with RF = 36 kΩ.
On products qualified to MIL-PRF-38535 every parameter is tested unless noted; on other products production testing does not necessarily cover every parameter.
TL062 and TL064 are catalog products; TL062M and TL064M are the military versions.
